findings.problem: Roughly 90 lines of nontrivial reasoning are duplicated in a second proof. The block covers: the hst/hst₁/hst₂ stability facts; the A, Sg, hcommH and hxA setup; the commutation and trivial-intersection bullets; and the le_antisymm argument showing that the centralizer is contained in A ⊔ Sg. The latter splits κ γ as a torus part times a rootSpan part, rewrites the torus part as z·q₀ using the ZGrp·rootSpan decomposition, applies fixed_of_mul_mem, pulls the two factors back with exists_reeConj_eq, and recombines. The same proof appears in `exists_decomp_gen` in ReeF4Big/Decomp.lean, which differs only in using a general prime p > 3 instead of 5 and in obtaining hsplit and hinf from the `_gen` lemmas instead of `rootDiagUnit_eq_mul_ZGrp` and `ZGrp_inf_rootSpan_eq_bot`. Any fix to one copy has to be made in the other.
findings.proposed_change: Add a core lemma to this file, `exists_decomp_core`, and make both users thin. Its hypotheses are the same as `exists_decomp_gen` except that, instead of u, J, hΦ, hsplit and hinfJ, it takes the S-level facts directly: `hsplitS : ∀ c, ∃ z ∈ ZGrp (L := L) (rootCharKernel b), ∃ q ∈ rootSpan ReeTag.F4.tag L (rootCharKernel b), rootDiagUnit ReeTag.F4.tag c = z * q` and `hinf : ZGrp (L := L) (rootCharKernel b) ⊓ rootSpan ReeTag.F4.tag L (rootCharKernel b) = ⊥`. It also takes (hp : p.Prime) (hp3 : 3 < p) and hbp with exponent p. Its conclusion is the first five conjuncts plus `x ∈ A`, without the Suzuki equivalence. The proof is the current proof of lines 92–184 with Nat.prime_five replaced by hp and `(by norm_num)` by `(by omega : p ≠ 2)`. `exists_decomp_of_kernel` then becomes: obtain u from `exists_b2_conj`; build hS; call the core with `rootDiagUnit_eq_mul_ZGrp hS u hΦ` and `ZGrp_inf_rootSpan_eq_bot hS u hΦ`; and add the equivalence bullet. `exists_decomp_gen` becomes the same call with `rootDiagUnit_eq_mul_ZGrp_gen hS u hΦ hsplit` and `ZGrp_inf_rootSpan_eq_bot_gen hS u hΦ hinfJ`.
findings.benefit: The decomposition argument is stated and maintained once, and each user shrinks to its genuinely different part: how the splitting and trivial-intersection facts are obtained, and the final equivalence. Readers no longer have to diff two ~90-line proofs to check they agree, and later changes to the argument (for example to fixed_of_mul_mem or mem_torus_mul_rootSpan_of_commute) need one edit.

findings.problem: The transport of a group isomorphism through the conjugation embedding κ is repeated, and it is also repeated in `sg_equiv_of` in ReeF4Big/Decomp.lean. In both, Sg is the preimage of rootSpan under reeConj. The proof computes Sg.map κ = rootSpan ⊓ twistedFixed via `map_comap_eq` and `range_reeConj`, then composes `equivMapOfInjective`, `subgroupCongr` and the given equivalence. The helper `sg_equiv_of` already exists but sits in the downstream file, so this file reproduces its body inline.

Its hypothesis is `hSgm : ∀ γ, γ ∈ Sg ↔ reeConj g₀ γ ∈ rootSpan ReeTag.F4.tag L S`, with an equivalence `G₀ ≃* ↥(rootSpan … S ⊓ twistedFixed D.F n)`.
